_comment: Approved excerpts: each row a passage of a bundled score that the build cuts into its own file
and catalogue item (E1; docs/03 §4c). Written by `python tools/content/excerpts.py --merge` from
the microscope's excerpt view (#/dev/microscope/excerpts) and read by the build; not edited by hand.
`fromBar`/`toBar` are **1-based positions in the printed score**: bar 1 is the first printed bar, a
pickup included — what `sections.json` counts and the model's `sourceMeasureIndex` counts from. A
range across a repeat sign, a first-or-second ending or a jump refuses at build, with the bars named.
`selection` is the hands the learner is given: `both`, `right` (the upper staff alone) or `left`.
`targets` are vocabulary skill or demand ids the passage was approved for, never an invented name.
`parentSha256` is the parent's built file the approval was made against: when the parent's file
changes the validator names the row as stale. `event`, `by` and `at` are the approving decision.
`cutVersion` is the cutter the approval was merged under (a row without one predates the field: version
1); an approval under an older cutter is stale by cut version, and nothing carries it to the new cut.
`rejected` keeps the refusals with their reasons, so a re-merge of the same export appends nothing.
`superseded` (written once there is one) keeps each approval a person re-decided after it went stale, by
parent bytes or by cut version, and each one a person's rejection withdrew while it was current: the old
row as it was, with `supersededBy`, the event that replaced it (a rejection is kept in `rejected` too). A
renewal names the parent's current bytes and is merged under the cutter in force; nothing renews by itself.
An excerpt is on no rung: placement is F's, on a candidate-rungs line established on the combined
build and a current `goodTeachingUse: yes` on the cut's identity in D2's record by a named reviewer.

excerpts.note: Boundary by rule, unheard. Signals: phrase start after the long note (D, a dotted half) that ends bar 24; ending at the piece’s last bar (the final repeat sign); no pickup before bar 25; key signature located 8 times in 8 bars (B-flats in bars 26, 28, 30 and 31, the window rule met); both hands in every bar; eight bars. Nothing untaught at classical.3, where the whole piece carries sixteenths and triplets. Read on the page: F major, 3/4, eighths over quarters, E-flat and F-sharp written in bars 25 and 27, a grace note before the last bar. Usable score by the notation; teaching use undecided.

Boundary by rule, unheard. Signals — opportunity: rhythm.syncopation: 7 located in 4 bars (meets the window rule: at least 3 and 0.25 a bar); occurrences: rhythm.syncopation in 4 of 4 bars; phraseStart: a double bar before bar 25; ending: a repeat sign closes bar 28; pickup: no upbeat before bar 25; texture: one staff; length: 4 bars. Read on the page: B-flat major, one staff with chord symbols (a lead sheet): eighth-note lines whose off-beat eighths are tied over the beat in every bar (F5, D5, C5, B-flat4, G4 each tied from the and of a beat), the syncopation by the first clause of T37’s definition, a note or tie starting off the beat. Usable score by the notation; teaching use undecided.

Signals — opportunity: texture.left-hand-pattern: every bar of 4; occurrences: texture.left-hand-pattern in 4 of 4 bars; phraseStart: a double bar before bar 9; ending: a double bar closes bar 12; pickup: no upbeat before bar 9; texture: both hands sound in 4 of 4 bars; length: 4 bars. Read on the page: G major, 4/4: the left hand strikes D2 on beat 1 and the chord D3 G3 B3 on beat 3 in bars 9–11, C-sharp3 then D3 F-sharp3 A3 in bar 12 — a bass note then a chord, the oom-pah in half notes; the right hand a stepwise tune in quarters and eighths; a double bar before bar 9 and after bar 12. Usable score by the notation; teaching use undecided.

Boundary by rule, unheard. Signals — opportunity: texture.walking-bass: every bar of 4; occurrences: texture.walking-bass in 4 of 4 bars; phraseStart: after a rest in the melody at the end of bar 14; ending: a double bar closes bar 18; pickup: no upbeat before bar 15; texture: both hands sound in 4 of 4 bars; length: 4 bars. Read on the page: B-flat major, 4/4: the left hand walks in single quarter notes on every beat — G2 B-flat2 D3 D-flat3, C3 G2 C2 E2, C2 E-flat2 G2 G-flat2, F2 A2 C3 E-flat2 — chord tones with chromatic approach notes, never a repeated or chordal bass; the right hand comps in chords off the beat, with rests; a double bar closes bar 18. The walk is read on the page, beside E22’s caution about the detector. Usable score by the notation; teaching use undecided.

Boundary by rule, unheard. Signals — opportunity: pitch.chromatic: 7 located in 4 bars (meets the window rule: at least 3 and 0.1 a bar); occurrences: pitch.chromatic in 2 of 4 bars; phraseStart: the piece's first bar; ending: resolves: a rest over the tonic in the bass; pickup: no pickup before bar 1; texture: one staff; length: 4 bars. Read on the page: B-flat major, one staff with chord symbols (a lead sheet): D5 and D-flat5 alternating in eighths through bars 1–2, each D-flat a flat outside the key and each D after it a natural sign, then C5 and D5 in halves and B-flat4 held into a rest. Usable score by the notation; teaching use undecided.

The habanera bass, left hand alone: printed bars 1-12, three bars of the bass alone and then the bass under the first sung phrase to the cadence on D at bar 12. Every bar's left-hand onsets are 0, 3/8, 1/2 and 3/4 of the 2/4 bar (the habanera cell: dotted eighth, sixteenth, two eighths), D2-A2-F3-A2 in bars 1-7 and 12, D2-B-flat2-G3-B-flat2 in bars 8-11; checked by two readers (partitura and a raw XML walk) on the archive file and the committed file, and no bar matches the tresillo set (latin.4 probe, cell check). No vocabulary id names the habanera; rhythm.sixteenths is the one existing demand the cell's defining onset is. Boundary by rule from the notation, not heard.

rejected.reason: The right hand repeats one dyad, F4 over A4, eight times in the four bars: the notes outside the key are one accidental read once and repeated, with no line to read. The signals are met; a passage the page shows as one repeated chord is left for a reviewer.

The syncopation the detector reads here is only T37’s clause for a bar whose melody opens on a rest: the right hand enters on beats 2 and 4 after the left hand on 1 and 3, the hands alternating on the beat; no note or tie starts off the beat in bars 1–8. The signals are met; a reading the detector’s definition gives by one clause alone is not approved as syncopation.

The vocabulary maps every left-hand pattern to one detector (claims.CONCEPT_DEMANDS: alberti, waltz, oom-pah, boogie, stride), which cannot tell them apart; the page can.
